prompt: Find the smallest positive angle coterminal with $1000^\circ$. Give just the number of degrees.
hint: Keep subtracting $360^\circ$ until what is left is between $0^\circ$ and $360^\circ$ — one subtraction may not be enough.

hints.text: Keep subtracting $360^\circ$ until what is left is between $0^\circ$ and $360^\circ$ — one subtraction may not be enough.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up with $800^\circ$: $800 - 360 = 440$, still over a full lap, so subtract again: $440 - 360 = 80^\circ$. That one needed two subtractions, and so does yours.
$1000 - 360 = 640$, which is still bigger than $360$. Subtract again.
$640 - 360 = 280$, and $280^\circ$ is between $0^\circ$ and $360^\circ$, so that is the answer.

explanation: Coterminal angles differ by whole turns of $360^\circ$, so subtract full turns until you land inside one lap.
$1000 - 360 = 640$; that is still more than a full turn, so subtract again: $640 - 360 = 280$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Divide instead of subtracting twice
steps: $1000 \div 360 = 2$ full turns with something left over.
Two full turns are $720^\circ$, so the leftover is $1000 - 720 = 280^\circ$.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: The tempting answer is $640^\circ$ — you subtracted $360^\circ$ once and stopped. But $640^\circ$ is still almost two full laps, so it is not the smallest.
Make the check part of the routine: after every subtraction, ask "is this now under $360$?" If not, subtract again. Only $280^\circ$ passes that test.
